content: @Damiano Testa, @Michael Rothgang (I think you are the relevant persons?), the new style linter for long lines has a pretty serious (IMO) regression in behavior compared to the old one: Since it generates warnings during the build, and the mathlib build errors on warnings, we don't get all the long line errors in the build at once, meaning that one needs to spend several CI cycles to shorten lines when previously all long lines were flagged simultaneously and could be fixed at once.
I was also thinking of adding back the old linter anyway, since the linter only flags long lines after the linter starts to be imported. Let me PR it back.
The only drawback that I see with the two linters working, is that exceptions need to be recorded twice. Since there is currently exactly one exception in Mathlib, this does not seem too onerous.

@Yaël Dillies Which CI run is this? lake build --wfail should not fail on warnings until the very end
Sorry, not at a computer right now but it's somewhere in #15177
There's an issue I just came across: the long line linter now fires in the author field of the copyright docstring, whereas previously it didn't.

Are you sure that it did not do that earlier? If not, it might have been a bug, since these lines are present in the linter

    -- if the linter reached the end of the file, then we scan the `import` syntax instead
    let stx := ← do
      if stx.isOfKind ``Lean.Parser.Command.eoi then
        let fileMap ← getFileMap
        -- `impMods` is the syntax for the modules imported in the current file
        let (impMods, _) ← Parser.parseHeader
          { inputString := fileMap.source, fileName := ← getFileName, fileMap := fileMap }
        return impMods.raw
      else return stx

They specifically instruct the linter to inspect the imports of the file, when elaboration reaches the end of the file.
What may have changed (this I have not checked) is whether the copyright preceding the imports was embedded into the parsed-import syntax.

This is a subtly technical point, but virtually all syntax has some trailing whitespace/comment, but it is very rare for syntax to embed whitespace/comment before itself. A clear exception is the first command of each file, which could be preceded by whitespace/comments, such as module.

So, it is possible that before the module system (or some other change affecting imports), the syntax of the imports forgot the header, which seems strange, but possible, and it is now embedding it in the header.
#36906 was a recent change to the long-lines linter around file headers, although it looks like it only removes errors rather than add some
I wrote that PR; I would be very surprised if it added errors.
Yeah the real cause of this is lean4#12662 and I'm pretty sure the change in general is intentional. The copyright comment analysis also allows ,<newline> ... to separate authors.
